description: OCS-Kit-Pages feature catalog: the single source of truth for which files of this site belong to which kit feature. Feature ids, names, categories, labels, roles and kit presets are copied verbatim from the canonical OCS-Kit/kits/catalog.json (scripts/apply_kit.py --sync-canonical; --check verifies). 'pages' is local: repo-relative files, folders (trailing /) or globs. Anything not listed is core and always built.
pages_help:
Paths use Jekyll exclude semantics (prefix or fnmatch glob). Derived outputs are excluded automatically: _notebooks/X -> _posts/X*, _posts/X.md -> course splits X_*, _projects/

-> every folder the project Makefile copies to. Shared layouts/includes stay core and are guarded in Liquid with site.data.kit.disabled.

feature_management.description: Only admins may enable, disable or configure features (admin dashboard or installer). Staff and members can see which features are on but cannot change them. Server operators can also set KIT/FEATURES in the backend .env files.

admin.description: Runs the site: manages users, roles and features. The only role that can turn features on or off.

staff.description: Runs day-to-day work: content, groups, grading or approvals. Cannot change features.

member.description: Regular user of the site. Default role for new sign-ups. Cannot change features.

general.name: General
general.description: Useful to any organization; included in Business and available to every kit.

education.name: Educational
education.description: Classroom-specific features (lessons, grading, hall pass). Included in the Education kit only; other kits can still opt in explicitly.

labels.student-safe: Fine to give to students without extra setup or supervision.
labels.classroom: Built for running a class (teacher/student roles, periods, courses).
labels.teacher-tools: Mainly used by teachers or admins.
labels.needs-api-key: Needs a third-party API key in the backend .env to work.
labels.third-party-data: Sends user content to an outside service (e.g. an AI provider).
labels.needs-external-service: Needs a separate server or account you run yourself.
labels.user-content: Users post content others can see; plan for moderation.
labels.privacy-sensitive: Handles sensitive data (e.g. biometrics); check your privacy policy first.
labels.runs-code: Executes user code in sandboxed containers.
labels.demo: Sample/teaching code, not needed in production.

core.name: Core platform
core.description: Login, accounts, roles, sections/groups, profile, admin pages, blog + notebook pipeline, search.

setup.summary: Works out of the box. Optional settings add email and Google sign-in for password resets, and S3 file storage.

settings.help: SMTP account used to send password-reset and notification emails.
Password or app password for that SMTP account.
Google OAuth client id for 'reset password with Google'.
S3 bucket for uploaded files (local disk is used when empty).

steps: Sign in as the admin account created by the installer and change its password.
Create sections/groups and invite users.
setup.verify: Sign in on the website and open your profile page.

core.notes: Everything not listed under another feature: index, login/logout/signup, profile, /dashboard (preferences), admin, blog, search, SASS guide, base layouts and includes.

lessons.name: Lessons
lessons.description: Course lessons and notebooks, lesson layouts, lesson progress tracking.

setup.summary: Lessons are part of the website. Optional text-to-speech needs a VoiceRSS key.

settings.help: VoiceRSS key for the 'read aloud' button in lessons.

steps: Add or edit lessons as Jupyter notebooks in _notebooks/ (or Markdown in _posts/) of your website repository.
Push to GitHub; the site rebuilds automatically.

code-runner.name: Code runners
code-runner.description: Run student Python, JavaScript and Java in sandboxed runner containers; code-runner widgets in lessons.

setup.summary: Runs inside the backend's code_runner containers, which the installer starts automatically.

settings.help: Address of the Java runner container (default http://code_runner:8592).

steps: Make sure the code_runner service is running: `docker compose ps` in the flask and spring folders.
setup.verify: Open a lesson with a code-runner cell and press Run.

code-runner.notes: Runner includes (_includes/runners/*) stay core because lessons embed them; with code-runner off they render plain code.

assignments.name: Assignments and grading
assignments.description: Assignments, submissions, grades, quizzes, quests, certificates, evaluations, team teaching, sprint dates, student/teacher toolkit, grade predictors.

setup.summary: Needs sections and students; optional GitHub tokens enable Gist/issue submissions.

settings.help: GitHub token for reading submitted repositories and issues.
GitHub token allowed to create Gists for code submissions.

steps: Create a section/course and add students (admin dashboard → Users).
Create an assignment with a due date and rubric.
Students submit from the assignment page; grade from the submissions view.
setup.verify: Create a test assignment and submit it with a student account.

assignments.notes: Submit buttons/forms (_includes/lesson-submit*.html, challenge-submit-button.html) stay core and render nothing when assignments is off.

game-engine.name: Game engine
game-engine.description: JavaScript game engine, game projects (gamify, adventure/RPG), multiplayer, leaderboards, AI NPCs.

setup.summary: Runs in the browser; no setup needed. One game level can show live market news with an AlphaVantage key.

settings.help: AlphaVantage key for the market-news game level (uses the limited 'demo' key when empty).

setup.verify: Open the games page and start a level.

game-engine.notes: images/gamify/ stays core: lessons (network stack) reuse its pictures.

ai-chatbot.name: AI chatbot
ai-chatbot.description: AI chatbot / tutor on the website, answered through the backend's Gemini or Groq chat proxy (API keys stay on the server).

setup.summary: Needs a Gemini (or Groq) API key on the Flask backend. Keys never go in the website.

settings.help: Google Gemini API key used by the chatbot.
Optional Groq key as an alternative model provider.

steps: Add the key to the Flask .env and restart: `docker compose up -d` in the flask folder.
Tell users that chat messages are sent to the AI provider.
setup.verify: Open the chatbot and send a message; it should answer instead of saying 'AI assistant not configured'.

ai-grading.name: AI grading
ai-grading.description: AI grading and feedback for free-response (FRQ) answers and assignments.

setup.summary: Needs a Gemini API key on the Spring backend (and Flask for submission summaries).

settings.help: Google Gemini API key used to grade free-response answers.
Same key on Flask, used to summarize submissions.

steps: Add the key to both .env files and restart both backends.
Review AI grades before releasing them to students.
setup.verify: Submit a free-response answer on a test assignment and check that feedback appears.

ai-grading.notes: No standalone pages on the website; lessonbase.html hides its AI grading block when ai-grading is off.

social.name: Social
social.description: Microblog, posts, comments, notes, announcements, chat and direct messages, personas.

setup.summary: Works out of the box. Decide who moderates posts before turning it on.

settings.help: Optional model endpoint for the 'chatter' feature (disabled when empty).

steps: Pick moderators (Admin or Teacher/Manager accounts) and tell users the posting rules.
setup.verify: Create a post with one account and see it from another.

social.notes: base.html only includes the microblog/inbox/feedback widgets when social is on; post comments (utterances) too.

setup.summary: Works out of the box. Optional Slack sync needs a Slack bot token.

settings.help: Slack bot/user token for syncing announcements and events.
owner:email pairs for issue notifications.

steps: Add your term dates and events from the calendar page.
setup.verify: Open the calendar page and add an event.

analytics.name: Analytics
analytics.description: Usage analytics, GitHub contribution stats, skill snapshots, stats dashboards.

setup.summary: Usage analytics work out of the box. GitHub statistics need a token and the org/user to track.

settings.help: GitHub token for contribution statistics.
'user' or 'organization'.
GitHub org or user whose activity is tracked.
Optional skill-snapshot service URL.

steps: Open the analytics dashboard as an Admin or Teacher/Manager.
setup.verify: The analytics dashboard shows activity after users sign in.

analytics.notes: head-custom.html only loads the analytics tracker when analytics is on.

hallpass.name: Hall pass
hallpass.description: Bathroom/hall pass queues, student help queue, approval requests.

setup.summary: Works out of the box once teachers exist.

settings.help: Owner of the default queues and contact address shown to students.

steps: Create Teacher accounts; each teacher gets a queue.
Share the hall-pass page with students.
setup.verify: Request a pass as a student and approve it as the teacher.

hallpass.notes: Hall pass pages are served by the backends; the website has no hall pass pages yet.

finance-sim.name: Finance simulation
finance-sim.description: Bank, stocks, crypto and mining simulation, casino-style probability games.

setup.summary: Runs with simulated data. Optional keys pull live prices.

settings.help: Live crypto prices.
Stock history API (simulated data when empty).

setup.verify: Open the finance pages and make a simulated trade.

resume.name: Resume builder
resume.description: Personal resume / profile pages and API.

steps: Tell users resumes are visible to signed-in users.
setup.verify: Create a resume from your profile.

resume.notes: Resume pages are served by the backends; the website has no resume pages yet.

kasm.name: Kasm virtual desktops
kasm.description: Kasm Workspaces integration (needs a Kasm server).

setup.summary: Needs your own Kasm Workspaces server.

settings.help: URL of your Kasm server.
Kasm API key.
Kasm API key secret.

steps: Install Kasm Workspaces on a separate server (https://kasmweb.com/docs).
Create an API key in Kasm admin → Developers.
setup.verify: Open the Kasm users admin page; it should list Kasm users.

face-recognition.name: Face recognition
face-recognition.description: Face registration/login (biometric data: check your school's privacy policy before enabling).

setup.summary: No keys needed, but it stores biometric data. Get consent first.
steps: Check your privacy policy and local law for biometric data; get written consent.
Serve the site over HTTPS (browsers only allow cameras on HTTPS).
setup.verify: Register a face on the profile page and sign in with it.

examples.name: Teaching examples
examples.description: Classroom demo code: hacks, jokes, small sample APIs and pages, media-literacy lesson.

setup.summary: No setup needed; sample code for teaching.

vanilla.name: OCS Vanilla
vanilla.description: Baseline site that can be handed to students: accounts, profile, blog and notebooks. Admins can add features later.

education.name: OCS Education
education.description: A full CS classroom: lessons, code runners, assignments and grading, game engine, AI chatbot tutor and AI grading, calendar, analytics, hall pass.

business.name: OCS Business
business.description: For companies and organizations serving their own users (no students): accounts with Admin/Manager/Member roles, AI chatbot, posts and messaging, calendar, analytics, profiles/resumes. Add any other feature (code runners, game engine, finance simulation, Kasm, face recognition) from the admin dashboard.
